epics.title: Phase 0: Foundations
epics.description: Site, gates, tracker, upstream pin, fixture corpus, golden generator, Cargo workspace and CI. Everything later phases depend on to be reproducible.

epics.title: Phase 1: Core model and file format (excali-core)
epics.description: Element types, serde with unknown-field preservation, restore/migration rules, AppState, fractional indexing, library formats, payload codecs, conformance corpus.

epics.title: Phase 2: Geometry and sketch renderer
epics.description: excali-math, excali-rough (rough.js 4.6.4 semantics), excali-freehand, the display list, and golden tests against upstream output.

epics.title: Phase 3: Text and fonts (excali-text)
epics.description: Font metadata, measurement from font files, wrapping port, bound-text sizing, lazy font assets with verified licences.

epics.title: Phase 4: Headless rendering and export
epics.description: tiny-skia raster backend, SVG writer, PNG/SVG payload embedding, CLI.

epics.title: Phase 5: Web runtime and editor
epics.description: Canvas2D backend, interaction state machine, history, DOM chrome without a framework, keyboard shortcuts, the <excali-editor> custom element.

epics.title: Phase 6: Host integration (term.hut and Tauri)
epics.description: Vendored module in term.hut with CRUD and library import; tauri-plugin-excali with dialogs, headless export and allow-listed fetch; example app.

epics.title: Phase 7: Parity and polish
epics.description: Tablet and phone layouts, remaining tools, accessibility, performance budgets, locale loader, parity checklist to 100%.

epics.title: Phase 8: Release
epics.description: First calendar release v26.9.1 (ADR-009): ES module + WASM tarball as a GitHub release asset, integration guide walked by an agent in a fresh clone, tag and gh release. crates.io publishing (ex-801) is deferred by the owner.

tasks.title: Platform-independent float maths: excali_math::js for every transcendental, std methods disallowed by clippy
tasks.acceptance: excali_math::js ports V8's fdlibm (src/base/ieee754.cc, with the fused multiply-adds clang emits on arm64) for sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, exp, log, log2, log10 and cbrt, keeps V8's Math.hypot, and answers pow with V8's special cases and the correctly rounded power; goldens/js-math.json (tools/goldens/js-math.mjs, Node at tools/goldens/.node-version on arm64) and crates/excali-math/tests/js_math.rs pin V8's bits for special values, every reduction path and arguments where fdlibm without FMA or the platform's libm is an ulp away; every f64/f32 transcendental call in crates/** and tools/** goes through excali_math::js and the workspace clippy.toml disallows the std methods (clippy -D warnings); the rust workflow runs cargo test on ubuntu (x86_64 and arm64) and macOS with every golden, corpus and parity test green, the golden harness comparing exactly; excali-core and excali-math build for wasm32; ADR-011 and the architecture overview record the rule.
evidence: ex-513: rotated bound text y = 247.5924092061952 on Linux against upstream's 247.59240920619527 (packages/excalidraw/tests/history.test.tsx:4396; glibc cos(90) is one ulp from V8's)
V8 14.6.202.34 src/base/ieee754.cc (fdlibm), src/numbers/ieee754.cc math::pow (platform pow), src/builtins/math.tq MathHypot
Node 26.10.0 arm64 against ieee754.cc built with clang -ffp-contract=on: equal on 400,000 random arguments per function (run 2026-09-28)
tools/goldens/README.md: the goldens are the arm64 output; x86_64 V8 differs in the last bits
tasks.description: Upstream runs on V8, whose Math transcendentals are V8's own fdlibm on every OS, while Rust's f64 methods call the platform libm, which differs by an ulp between macOS and glibc. Port V8's code into excali_math::js, replace every std call, disallow the std methods in clippy.toml, run the test suite on macOS and Linux, and record the rule in an ADR and the architecture overview.

tasks.title: Attribution gate self-test in CI: a planted attribution line must fail the gate
tasks.acceptance: scripts/gates/test_attribution.py builds a scratch git repo in a temp dir and plants, one at a time: a tool-attribution line in a tracked file, a Co-Authored-By trailer in a commit message (commit-tree, no hooks involved), a zero-width character, and a non-human author; each case asserts `attribution.py files --all` or `attribution.py history` exits non-zero with the rule id, and a clean control case exits 0.
